title: 视觉研究方向近期重点论文速览
summary: 过去24小时至7天内，视觉研究呈现两条主线：一是面向物理一致性的视频与世界模型，强调几何控制、动作后果评测与生成可靠性；二是三维重建与高斯渲染，在动态场景、拓扑变化与异质相机适配上持续扩展。此外，可控生成与多模态具身视觉在评测和方法层面均有代表性工作。
highlights: BWM-Forge 用代码驱动场景编程实现机器人视频可控生成
WanderBench 系统评测视频世界模型的探索保真度
Topo-4DGS 面向自我中心视频的拓扑变化动态重建
Camera3R 以低秩适配扩展基础重建模型到异质相机
markdown:
## BWM-Forge: Agentic World Programming for Embodied Intelligence
[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16221)
研究问题：机器人视频生成需要同时控制场景几何、机器人运动与视角，端到端模型难以直接编辑这些变量。方法上，该工作用编码智能体构造可编辑的 Blender 场景程序，生成代理视频作为结构参考，再由视频生成模型补全视觉细节，并用多智能体流程协调输入处理、场景构建、审查与渲染。证据显示其在覆盖五类机器人、15 项任务的评测中与基线比较，说明共享场景程序支持多视角同步与外观变化；具体数值指标输入未完整给出。适用场景为具身数据合成与可控世界模型训练；限制在于依赖 Blender 场景搭建质量。代码状态未核实。

## WanderBench: Can World Models Explore Dynamic Worlds from Video?
[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12557)
研究问题：视频条件的世界模型能否在探索录制场景时保持主体身份、事件推进与重访一致性。该工作构建 745 段单镜头源视频、三级难度与键盘相机路线，使用 24 个经人工验证的子指标评测八个模型。结果表明随片段变长，模型保持静态场景与画质却丢失相机控制与源动态，且无一模型能维持重访地点一致；作者另提出免训练框架 WanderLand。适用场景为真实视频重拍与 real-to-sim；限制是基准以评测为主，方法改进范围有限。代码状态未核实。

## Topology-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Egocentric Videos
[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16012)
研究问题：单目自我中心视频中切割、装配、开合等拓扑变化会使依赖固定形变的 4DGS 产生严重伪影。Topo-4DGS 为交互部件分配独立刚体变换，并随时间动态激活或停用高斯，以建模部件级运动与时变表面支撑；同时提出 TopoEgo 基准覆盖分裂、融合、打开与关闭。实验显示其在拓扑变化、尤其是事件后帧上明显优于现有 4DGS 方法。适用场景为具身交互重建；限制是依赖部件级建模假设。代码与数据称将公开，当前未核实。

## Camera3R: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Heterogeneous Camera Models
[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13453)
研究问题：透视数据预训练的前馈三维重建模型难以泛化到非透视与异质相机。Camera3R 采用低秩适配框架，仅增加约 0.5% 参数、训练不足一天，即可将基础重建网络扩展到其他相机模型，同时保留原透视输入性能。该工作提供代码链接，复现性相对明确。适用场景为任意未知相机模型的多视图重建；限制是适配范围取决于基础模型能力。

## Library of Hands: Fix the Hands, Not the World Model
[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12678)
研究问题：相机移动或控制器更换会改变命令到实际动作的映射，冻结世界模型的规划器在命令旋转 90 度时成功率从 77.5% 骤降至 7.8%。LoH 保持世界模型冻结，仅通过冻结模型从两帧图像读取并校正"手"映射，并存储已识别配置以识别回归场景。闭环测试中三个模拟任务成功率由 28.6% 提升至 62.3%，环境不变时仅损失 0.6 个百分点，并可迁移到另外两个世界模型。适用场景为部署条件变化下的机器人规划；限制是依赖读取质量。代码状态未核实。

## UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16517)
研究问题：统一多模态模型需兼顾理解与生成的注意力效率。UniSpark-9B 在混合 Transformer 专家骨干上结合全注意力与 GatedDeltaNet 线性注意力，联合自回归文本预测与视觉流匹配，并用分块协议隔离含噪视觉目标与干净上下文。训练数据含 1.597 亿生成样本、2.134 亿理解样本与 62.48 万交错序列，四阶段课程将图像合成扩展至 2K。适用场景为交错图文生成与编辑；限制是模型规模大、复现成本高。代码状态未核实。

papers.title: BWM-Forge: Agentic World Programming for Embodied Intelligence
papers.summary: Generating diverse robot videos requires control over scene geometry, robot motion, and viewpoints. End-to-end video generation offers limited direct access to these variables, making targeted edits and reuse across tasks difficult. We present BWM-Forge, a code-driven framework for controllable video generation in robotics. Given robot assets and a task description, the framework accepts an initial image, an image with motion data, or a human demonstration video. A coding agent constructs editable Blender scene programs that specify objects, robot motion, and cameras. The resulting proxy videos provide structural and motion references for a video generation model, which adds visual detail. A multi-agent harness coordinates input processing, scene construction, review, and rendering. Automated evaluation and user feedback support iterative refinement, while an experience repository stores and retrieves reusable modeling and rendering rules. This design supports multiple robot embodiments, synchronized viewpoints, and appearance variation from a shared scene program. We evaluate the framework on 15 tasks covering five robot types. papers.title: WanderBench: Can World Models Explore Dynamic Worlds from Video?
papers.summary: Video world models conditioned on an input video make it possible to explore real, recorded dynamic scenes, enabling re-shooting of footage, free-viewpoint replay, and real-to-sim environments for embodied agents. Such uses require the generated rollout to stay faithful to the recorded world, yet existing benchmarks start from a single image or a text prompt, and video-conditioned generation is evaluated mainly on perceptual quality and camera following. These evaluations do not directly assess whether exploration preserves subject identity, event progression, and scene consistency upon revisiting a location. We introduce WanderBench, a benchmark for exploring dynamic worlds from video. It comprises 745 single-shot source videos of real and AI-generated content in three difficulty tiers (3-25 s), paired with camera routes given as keyboard actions, and evaluates six dimensions with 24 human-validated sub-metrics. Benchmarking eight models, we find that as clips grow longer, models keep the static scene and visual quality but lose camera control and the source dynamics, and that none keeps revisited places consistent. papers.title: Topology-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Egocentric Videos
papers.summary: Reconstructing dynamic scenes and objects from monocular egocentric video is crucial for embodied AI, yet existing 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) approaches struggle with everyday interactions involving topological changes, such as cutting, assembly, opening, or closing. Since 4DGS methods rely on deforming a fixed representation, events that split, merge, or reveal surfaces cause severe visual artifacts. To address this challenge, we introduce TopoEgo, the first benchmark dedicated to topological changes in egocentric video (covering fission, fusion, open, and close), alongside Topo-4DGS, a topology-aware reconstruction method. Topo4DGS jointly models part-level motion and time-varying surface support by assigning independent rigid transformations to interacting parts and dynamically activating or deactivating Gaussians as surfaces appear, disappear, or separate. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Topo-4DGS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art 4DGS approaches across topological changes, especially on post-event frames. Code and data will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Camera3R: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Heterogeneous Camera Models
papers.summary: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction (3R) from unconstrained multi-view images has recently emerged as a prominent research direction in 3D computer vision. Various foundational reconstruction models have been proposed with different architectures and reconstruction paradigms. Despite being trained on large-scale perspective datasets with substantial computational resources, these models generally struggle to generalize to non-perspective images. This limitation hinders their deployment in applications involving arbitrary, unknown, and potentially heterogeneous camera models. To build on the capabilities of existing reconstruction models with minimal retraining, we propose Camera3R, a low-rank adaptation framework that efficiently extends perspective-pretrained 3R networks to any other camera models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, with only 0.5% additional parameters and less than a day of training, Camera3R adapts a foundational 3D reconstruction model to non-perspective cameras while fully preserving its original performance on perspective inputs. Code is available at https://github.com/android-xr/camera3r.

papers.title: Library of Hands: Fix the Hands, Not the World Model
papers.summary: A world model predicts how a scene changes after an action, and a planner uses it to search for actions that reach a goal. If the camera moves or the controller changes, the same command moves the robot differently: when its commands are turned by 90 degrees, a frozen planner with the LeWM world model that succeeds in 77.5% of episodes succeeds in only 7.8%. Current fixes retrain the model, need training data, or forget a set-up when it returns. We propose Library of Hands (LoH), a training-free method that keeps the world model frozen and corrects only the map from commands to applied actions, which we call the hand. LoH reads the hand through the frozen model, with no extra sensor: it finds the action that best explains the change between two camera images (a reading). It stores every hand it identifies, so a returning set-up is recognised rather than re-learnt. In closed-loop tests, LoH more than doubles success on three simulated tasks, from 28.6% to 62.3%, and loses only 0.6 percentage points when nothing changes. It also works, unchanged, with two other world models and on two of three models pretrained on real robot data, and its gain grows with the quality of its readings.

papers.title: UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
papers.summary: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. Autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching jointly support visual question answering, text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and interleaved text-image prediction. In interleaved generation, noisy visual targets are isolated from subsequent predictions, while clean visual representations provide context for later outputs. A blockwise protocol enforces this distinction through attention masks in full-attention layers and recurrent-state retention rules in linear-attention layers. The selected training sources contain 159.7M generation samples, 213.4M understanding samples, and 624.8K interleaved sequences. A four-stage curriculum jointly trains multimodal understanding and visual generation, refining answer accuracy and instruction following while extending image synthesis to 2K. UniSpark scores 2470.
